title: PHI Schema Check fact document
description: What the local inspector observed in one project root, sent to the evaluator once per call. Identifiers, enums, integers, booleans, hashes, rule ids and path:line locations only: no code, no values, no free text. Every object is closed. Version 2 is contract v1.1: the inspector sends schema_version 2. Limits checked before parsing: 5,000,000 bytes, depth 12, 20,000 items per array. Anything the inspector didn't observe is absent or reported by its collector's status, never sent as a default that reads as clean.

ruleset_id.description: The rule bundle's manifest ruleset_id the inspector ran (rule_bundle.md). The evaluator accepts only its current one; otherwise update_inspector.

root_id.description: HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the per-install key, of the root's absolute path (forward slashes, no trailing slash), lowercase hex. Stable on one machine, never comparable across installs.

collection.description: One entry per collector, each at most once. A collector with no entry is read as failed.

files.description: analyzed: the number of files parsed and run through every rule for their language and frameworks.

not_analyzed.description: Every walked file or directory that could hold evidence but wasn't analysed, with why. kind directory: a whole directory skipped (path names the directory, no trailing slash), with tracked: yes when git tracks something under it, no when nothing (ignored or untracked), not_checked when the tracked set couldn't be read; tracked is null on file entries. A skipped directory counts against coverage for every language that could be in it. The one exception is excluded_directory, which only a folder skipped by name carries (enums.EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES, by its last path segment): version-control metadata (.git, .hg, .svn; enums.VCS_METADATA_DIRECTORIES) never blocks a coverage pass, where .git and .hg are only the root's own (path exactly .git or .hg): a nested .git or .hg is a nested repository, listed as embedded_git_dir, never excluded_directory, and an excluded_directory entry naming one is read as blocking; any other such folder (dependencies, environments, caches, package stores, build output, vendored code; enums.DEPENDENCY_DIRECTORIES) is exempt only with tracked no, and blocks with tracked yes or not_checked, since a tracked folder can hold app code whatever its name (the inspector walks a tracked one instead). Nested roots are reported with submodule, embedded_git_dir, gitlink_into_source or gitlink_to_ancestor (a gitlink naming the root or an ancestor, never followed). Over 20,000: the list stops and the files collector is truncated with item_limit.

frameworks.description: Frameworks detected from the project's manifests and imports.

fingerprints.description: Optional (T18). Kinds of service the project declares in its manifests and marker files, or imports in its source: ai_sdk, object_storage_sdk, realtime_sdk, error_tracking_sdk, firebase_sdk and vector_store_sdk (T23 B33: Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Chroma, Milvus, pgvector and other vector-store client libraries) from dependencies and imports; android, ios and flutter from native app manifests; mobile_hybrid from Capacitor, Cordova, Ionic, NativeScript, .NET MAUI and Kotlin Multiplatform (T23 B31a). Presence rests on a declared dependency, an import or a marker file. An empty list means none of these kinds was declared or imported, never that the code makes no such call (supabase-js and Rails carry realtime with no realtime_sdk). Absent when a manifest couldn't be read or parsed: then the fingerprint is unknown.

imports.description: Optional (T23 B31a). Evidence only: for each fingerprint the inspector's import scan saw in JavaScript, TypeScript or Python source, the package that gave it and its first import (path and line). Specifiers are normalised to their package name, and only names in the inspector's SDK tables are listed. Presence only: a fingerprint with no entry was not seen in an import, never that the code doesn't use it. Absent when the inspector ran no import scan.

derived_frameworks.description: Optional (T23 B31b). Frameworks the inspector derived from its import scan (specifiers normalised to package names, then the framework tables) and from paths (supabase/functions/<name>/ or supabase/migrations/ gives supabase), kept apart from files.frameworks, which comes from manifests. Rule coverage counts one for a language only when files.imports_dynamic is sent and its count for that language is 0. The observed absence never reads it. Absent when the inspector ran no import scan.

imports_dynamic.description: Optional (T23 B31b). For each language the import scan read, the number of require() and import() calls whose argument is not a literal string. Code loaded that way is invisible to the rules, so a derived framework doesn't cover a language with a count above 0. A language the scan didn't read has no key. Sent with files.derived_frameworks.

helpers.description: Optional (T23 B31b, T23-P1-C114). Each JavaScript, TypeScript or Python module whose exported functions do elevated or patient-scoped work: a client that skips row-level security (createClient with a service-role or secret key, the Firebase Admin SDK), object storage, or a write. Read lexically, with the import scan. functions lists its exported functions (the first 50, by name). importers lists every analysed file that imports it, directly or through other local modules (relative specifiers, and @/ or ~/ from the root or src/); importers_complete is false when that list was cut at 1000. A handlers practice gives a module that no file holding one of its handlers reaches a needs_review result of its own (helper_not_reached_from_handlers). Sent with files.derived_frameworks, and left out when the scan didn't read every file of these languages.

elevated_imports.description: Optional (T27-P1-C78, F3.2). Each analysed file (entry files included; tests, mocks, migrations, seeds, scripts and 'use client' files left out) that names a binding it imports, through local imports, from a module that makes an elevated client itself (createClient or create_client in a file naming a service-role or secret key, or the Firebase Admin SDK). line: the first line after the import that names the binding. module: that module. depth: 1 when the binding comes from it directly, more through barrels and helpers. One row per path and module, the nearest depth; sorted by path, then module; the first 500. A side-effect import or a re-export alone gives no row. Sent with files.derived_frameworks, and left out when the scan didn't read every file of these languages, as files.helpers.

elevated_imports_complete.description: Optional (T27-P1-C78, C73). false when files.elevated_imports was cut at 500 rows; sent with it.

manifests.description: Optional (T23 B56f). The package manifests and lockfiles the walk listed, by ecosystem: one entry per ecosystem with at least one, its count, and the first 20 paths by path order. The basenames come from the inspector's name rules (rule_bundle.md section 9). Metadata only: no file is opened, and neither contents nor sizes are sent. Every walked path is listed, docs, examples, tests and vendored folders included; the evaluator decides which count. An empty list means the walk listed none. Absent when a skipped directory could hide one or the walk stopped at its file limit: then the manifests are unknown.

env_files.description: .env* files by name and git standing. A tracked one is scanned for secrets locally by the inspector, like any other file, and sends only what the secrets array carries, never a value. An untracked or ignored one is never opened. A not_checked one is never opened either, and makes the secrets collector truncated (unreadable), so a clean scan can't be claimed.

data_files.description: Data-shaped files (database dumps, CSV, Parquet, JSON lines, archives) by name and size only; never opened. The kind comes from the inspector's name rules (rule_bundle.md section 8). tracked: whether git tracks it; not_checked when the tracked set couldn't be read (never read as no). Over 1,000: the list stops and the files collector is truncated with item_limit.

matches.description: Every match of a structural rule. kind evidence or violation: what the rule says it is. kind item: one in-scope item of an items rule, has_control saying whether it satisfies the rule's control. has_control is null for evidence and violation. line_end >= line_start (strict intake checks it). fingerprint: HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the per-install key, of rule_id, path and the matched node's text with whitespace runs collapsed to one space, joined by newlines; lowercase hex. table: the table the matched code reads or writes when the rule captures it, as the code names it: schema.name when the code qualifies it, a bare name when it doesn't (never a guessed schema); each part, quoted or unquoted, sent as written (quotes removed) when it fits pg_name, else hashed (u_ plus 16 hex); the evaluator compares table names case-insensitively and reads one matching no catalog table as unknown, never as a non-patient table; null when the rule captures no table. handler: HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the per-install key, over the UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify([path, name, startLine, startColumn]) for the enclosing function (line 1-based, column as the inspector's parser reports it; enums.HANDLER_ID_FIELDS), lowercase hex: an opaque id, unique per function, that links a match to links[]; an allowlisted callback (map, forEach, then, ...) takes its enclosing function's id; null when the match is in no function, in an unrecognised registration or wrapper, or the rule captures none. shared_fingerprint (contract 2.3 section 3.5): HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the project's content key from .custosa/state.json, of SHARED_FP_VERSION, rule_id, path and the inspector's walk of the matched node, joined by U+001F; lowercase hex. It is the same on every machine of the project, and it changes with an edit to what the node does, not with its formatting. null when the root has no content key or the walk's self-check failed; any null among a practice's projected matches gives no_content_key.

catalog.description: The Postgres catalog as phisc_ro reads it.

preflight.description: Run first, in code, as Player 2's A4 preflight (P2-213) plus write_privileges. role: current_user (the role name, never a user's identity); session_user: session_user; database: current_database(); system_identifier: pg_control_system()'s, as text (null when not executable); together they tie the facts to one cluster and database. settings_mismatched: pinned session settings that differ. superuser, bypassrls, replication, createrole: any role the session or current user can become has it. readable_tables: relations outside pg_catalog and information_schema any such role can SELECT (table or any column), except those only PUBLIC can read. public_readable_tables: relations only PUBLIC can read that no extension owns, reported and never failing (T27-P1-C60 F5); absent from an older inspector. writable_tables: the count of objects any such role (directly or through any membership) could change: relations in any schema, the catalog included, with INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES or TRIGGER, or MAINTAIN on PG17+ (table or any column); sequences with USAGE or UPDATE; large objects owned or with UPDATE; non-temp schemas and the current database with CREATE; pg_default_acl entries granting such a role or PUBLIC any of those privileges (USAGE for sequences, CREATE for schemas); USAGE on a foreign server or foreign data wrapper; and CREATEDB held by any such role. Not counted: core's PUBLIC UPDATE on pg_catalog.pg_settings, CREATE on a tablespace; SECURITY DEFINER writers stay report-only (definer_functions_executable). On Postgres 14 or earlier, or a database upgraded from one, public grants CREATE to PUBLIC, so setup tells the person to run REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC (enums.PREFLIGHT_SETUP_STEPS), after granting CREATE on public to the app or migration role that relies on it. extension_relations_readable: relations an extension owns that only PUBLIC can read (listed, never failing). catalog_tables, predefined_roles, dangerous_functions: the refused ones it can read, is a member of, or can execute. catalog_extensions: extensions installed in pg_catalog other than plpgsql and pg_cron. owned_objects: relations, schemas, functions and types outside the catalog, and the database, any such role owns. large_objects: it can read a large object or lo_compat_privileges is on. definer_functions_executable: SECURITY DEFINER functions outside the catalog it can execute; report only, never failing (the evaluator marks data-access practices needs_review while it is above 0). failed: the check ids that failed, in the order run; passed only when none did. Missing values fail closed: with no connection every field is null and failed is ["connect"]. writable_beyond_public (T29-P1-C189 item 3): writable_tables less the writes PUBLIC alone holds, counted part by part (every such role is a member of PUBLIC, so 0 means every write path is a grant to PUBLIC); public_write_defaults: pg_default_acl entries granting PUBLIC a write privilege; public_schema_create: PUBLIC may CREATE in schema public. All three are optional (absent from an older inspector) and null when not read; they never make the preflight pass.

queries.description: One result per catalog query, each at most once. A query with no entry is read as failed. Without a passed preflight no query may report rows.

platform.description: The database host's own settings, read through its API with the optional read token. Its status is the platform collection entry (the one source); unless that entry is ok, empty or truncated, every setting is not_read.

settings.description: verify_queries.PlatformRow's settings, then contract v1.1's. Each reads on when the control is in place. not_offered: the provider has no such setting; not_read: it wasn't read.

high_compliance.description: Supabase only (HIPAA high-compliance add-on). No API reads it: always not_read on Supabase and not_offered elsewhere, and it never counts against the platform collector's ok.

password_min_length_15.description: on: the auth platform's minimum password length is at least 15 (NIST, password alone).

password_min_length_8.description: on: the minimum password length is at least 8 (NIST, when a second factor is required).

login_rate_limited.description: on: the auth platform rate-limits sign-in attempts.

org_mfa_enforced.description: on: the hosting organization requires MFA of every member (staff accounts).

sso_idp_mfa.description: on: the configured SSO identity provider requires MFA.

storage_encrypted.description: on: Supabase Storage objects are encrypted at rest as the platform reports it.

functions_verify_jwt.description: on: every deployed Supabase Edge Function has verify_jwt on.

realtime_private_only.description: on: Supabase Realtime allows private channels only (public access off).

storage_public_access_blocked.description: on: object storage blocks public access account-wide (S3 Block Public Access, GCS public access prevention, Azure allowBlobPublicAccess false).

cloudsql_pgaudit_masking.description: on: Cloud SQL's pgaudit flags mask statement parameters.

firestore_backups_scheduled.description: on: Firestore has a backup schedule.

log_export.description: on: every in-scope instance's database logs are exported to a destination the team controls, as evaluator_api.md section 1.7 defines per provider (enums.LOG_SETTING_PROVIDERS; gcp also needs the Cloud SQL Data Access audit config on in the effective policy, the union of the project's and every ancestor folder's and the organization's audit configs (an ancestor whose policy couldn't be read is not_read), firebase reads the gcp definition). A filter not shown to cover the logs is not_read. Any other provider: not_offered.

log_retention.description: on: for every in-scope instance, at least one destination receiving all of its in-scope logs keeps them for any retention period of a day or more, or never deletes them (owner D8: no 365-day floor), as evaluator_api.md section 1.7 defines per provider (gcp's _Default bucket only with its retention observed; an Azure storage account only with a lifecycle policy read that deletes nothing within a day; an event hub's own retention is read but never settles the setting, since what consumes it can't be read). off when some instance has no event hub among its destinations, every one of its destinations was read, there is at least one, and none keeps them a day; not_read when no destination qualifies and one couldn't be read, or an instance's destinations include an event hub. supabase: always not_offered (its retention isn't observable). Any other provider: not_offered.

secrets.description: Secrets found in memory; never the value. fingerprint: HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the per-install key over the UTF-8 bytes of "custosa-secret-fingerprint-v1\0" (the text then a NUL byte; enums.SECRET_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX) followed by the secret, 64 lowercase hex. For a PEM key, the secret is the first 4,096 characters (enums.PEM_FINGERPRINT_CHARS) of the normalised base64 body: armour headers (the BEGIN and END lines and any Key: value header lines), comment prefixes and whitespace removed. For secrets.config-password, secrets.supabase-service-role-config and secrets.url-userinfo-password (enums.SECRET_LOCATION_RULES) the fingerprint is of the location instead, never the value: HMAC-SHA256 with the same key over the UTF-8 bytes of "custosa-secret-location-v1\0" (enums.SECRET_LOCATION_PREFIX) followed by the rule name (rule_id without secrets.), a NUL byte, the path as sent, a NUL byte and the line in decimal. in_history: whether the same secret is in committed history (not_checked when history wasn't read).

fingerprint.description: evaluator_api.md section 1.7: HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the per-install key over the UTF-8 bytes of "custosa-secret-fingerprint-v1\0" (the text then a NUL byte; enums.SECRET_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX) followed by the secret, 64 lowercase hex. For a PEM key, the secret is the first 4,096 characters (enums.PEM_FINGERPRINT_CHARS) of the normalised base64 body: armour headers (the BEGIN and END lines and any Key: value header lines), comment prefixes and whitespace removed. For secrets.config-password, secrets.supabase-service-role-config and secrets.url-userinfo-password (enums.SECRET_LOCATION_RULES) the fingerprint is of the location instead, never the value: HMAC-SHA256 with the same key over the UTF-8 bytes of "custosa-secret-location-v1\0" (enums.SECRET_LOCATION_PREFIX) followed by the rule name (rule_id without secrets.), a NUL byte, the path as sent, a NUL byte and the line in decimal.

answers.description: The assistant's answers to the evaluator's questions, relayed by the inspector. Graded E4, or E3 when the answer is here and location_kind is the kind the question expected. location and location_kind are set only for answers that carry a location, and location is null when location_kind is not_found or not_checked (an unconfirmed path is never forwarded). object_id must be one the evaluator issued in a question this session. answer is an enum per question_id (the table in evaluator_api.md section 1.5, enums.ANSWERS). Contract 2.2 (T23 B49): a here answer may also carry code (one of the practice's codes) and at (the located spans: one location or a list of them, each checked like location); both are accepted and not yet graded.

links.description: Which handler reads or writes which table, from rules that capture both (each pair once per access). handler is matches[].handler's id; table as matches[].table names it. Present only as far as the rules collector ran: its status is the rules entry's.

columns.description: The inspector's name-and-type classifier over the catalog's columns: exactly one entry per table_columns row (table = schema_name.table_name, same column and type) while that query is ok or truncated, and none otherwise (strict intake checks it). The recognisers live in the inspector; only the class is sent. unknown: no recogniser matched; it goes to the person, never read as technical.

tenancy.description: How tenants are separated. source observed: the inspector derived it from the catalog it read; graded E2 (a derivation) with the worst status of the catalog collector, rls_policies and table_columns; allowed only while the catalog collector is ok or truncated, never with model single, and (strict intake) for row_level only with at least one rls_policies row whose tenant_comparison is true, and a tenant_column that appears in table_columns. answer: the assistant said so (E4); single comes only from an answer. tenant_column is set only for row_level, and may be null there when it couldn't be named.

supabase.description: Supabase project configuration the inspector parsed from the repository (contract v2.1).

edge_functions.description: The Edge Functions declared in supabase/config.toml, parsed by the inspector on the machine (TOML is config, not code). status follows the collection rules: not_run with not_configured when the walk found no supabase/config.toml; failed with parse_failed when any one the walk found wasn't parsed (unreadable, too large, not valid TOML, skipped by the walk), even if another parsed; truncated with item_limit past 1,000 functions (or size_limit). The reason is tied to the status (enums.EDGE_FUNCTIONS_STATUS_REASONS): not_run only with not_configured, failed with parse_failed, internal_error or, when the walk itself failed, the files collector's reason (timeout, not_permitted, ...; enums.FILES_COLLECTOR_REASONS, never not_configured, item_limit or size_limit), truncated with item_limit or size_limit; parse_failed is allowed nowhere else. Items only while ok or truncated (ok has at least one), none otherwise. Read with the files collector's status (worst of); a 'no config.toml' reading counts only after a complete walk. A supabase/config.toml named in files.not_analyzed, or, while the status is not_run, by a match of any practice, contradicts the list and is read as unknown (the evaluator reads it from the whole document, before narrowing matches to one practice).

cited_facts.description: T29 line item h (T29-P3-C85): facts the assistant reported for authz-every-handler (rule authz), write-fields-allowlisted (write_fields) and rls-policies-scoped (rls), relayed by the inspector, never a verdict. One row per field of a candidate: an authz or write_fields candidate is the handler's location, an rls candidate a table. value is the field's closed value (enums.FACT_VALUES) or unknown; for per_user_columns it is listed, with the columns in column_names ([] for none), and column_names is [] on every other field. cite is the inspector's check of the assistant's citation: ok when the file is in the walk, the line exists and the cited token (3 or more characters) is on that line; failed when not; none when no citation was given. cited_at is the cited file and line for ok and null otherwise; the token never leaves the machine. The names here are inline patterns, not the name $defs, and the keys are this section's own, so it adds no snapshot id (app.core.snapshot) and binds no ref. Optional: absent means the assistant sent no facts, and the three practices are judged as before (enums.FACT_RULES).

identifier.description: A name (or part) outside this pattern, a dotted name included, is sent hashed, never dropped: u_ plus the first 16 lowercase hex digits of HMAC-SHA256 (per-install key) over its UTF-8 bytes as Postgres prints it; the row stays and the query stays ok.

hashed_identifier.description: The form of a hashed name (see identifier). Fits every name pattern; the report shows it and the person maps it back locally.

path.description: Relative to the root, forward slashes, no leading / or ./, no . or .. segment, case preserved. A segment outside the allowed characters is sent as u_ plus 16 hex of HMAC-SHA256 (per-install key) over its UTF-8 bytes, and the file is still analysed; a path still over 512 characters is sent as one such hash of the whole path.

location.description: <path>:<n> or <path>:<n>-<m>. Strict intake also requires n <= m and m - n < 30.

object_id.description: The practice id alone, or <practice_id>@<object>, where the object is an identifier, a qualified name or a path and may hold @ and : (contract v1.1).

pg_name.description: A name (or part) outside this pattern, a dotted name included, is sent hashed, never dropped: u_ plus the first 16 lowercase hex digits of HMAC-SHA256 (per-install key) over its UTF-8 bytes as Postgres prints it; the row stays and the query stays ok.

qualified_name.description: schema.name. Each part outside the alphabet is hashed on its own (see pg_name).

bucket_id.description: A name (or part) outside this pattern, a dotted name included, is sent hashed, never dropped: u_ plus the first 16 lowercase hex digits of HMAC-SHA256 (per-install key) over its UTF-8 bytes as Postgres prints it; the row stays and the query stays ok.

data_type.pattern: ^(?:character varying|bit varying|double precision|(?:timestamp|time)(?:\([0-6]\))? with(?:out)? time zone|interval(?: (?:year|month|day|hour|minute|second)(?: to (?:month|hour|minute|second))?)?|"?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]{0,62}"?(?:\."?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]{0,62}"?)?)(?:\([0-9]{1,4}(?:,[0-9]{1,4})?\))?(?:\[\])*$
data_type.description: format_type() output. A type that fits none of these forms is sent hashed as one name (see pg_name).

setting.description: A server setting's value. One outside this pattern leaves its row out with value_out_of_pattern (not hashed: it is a value, not a name).

collection_status.description: ok: collected in full; empty: collected, nothing there; truncated: collected in part (never enough for a coverage pass); failed: tried and failed; not_run: not attempted. A missing status is read as failed.

collection_entry.description: One collector's outcome. count: files walked (files), tracked files read (git), rules run (rules), queries that returned rows or none (catalog), settings read (platform), secrets found (secrets). reason is null for ok and empty and required otherwise. parse_failed is never a collector's reason (supabase.edge_functions only); the A5 reasons (enums.SECRETS_TRUNCATED_REASONS: scan_error, joined_view_budget, bad_input, unreadable, match_cut_at_window) only the secrets collector's, while truncated: a file the secret scan didn't read in full. nothing_read (enums.RULES_ONLY_REASONS) only the rules collector's, while truncated: the rule engine read none of the files it had rules for (each is in files.not_analyzed), so the matches can't be read as found nothing.

environment.description: Which environment this is. source setup: the person flagged the phisc entry at setup; answer: the assistant said so (graded E4). Production readiness is judged only with value production from source setup. unknown when neither said.

query_rls_status.description: The rls_status query's result (up to 10000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/rls_status.sql (C1).

roles.description: The roles the policy applies to (pg_policy.polroles); public for PUBLIC.

owner_comparison.description: Derived, kept for compatibility: the tri-state OR of owner_using and owner_with_check (true when either is true, false when both are false, not_read otherwise). The comparison is a column of the row compared with the session's user (a trusted source is one of enums.TRUSTED_OWNER_SOURCES: auth.uid(), auth.jwt() ->> 'sub', current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub'), current_setting('request.jwt.claims') ->> 'sub'; the database role name, CURRENT_USER, CURRENT_ROLE, SESSION_USER or USER (enums.UNTRUSTED_OWNER_SOURCES), or any other setting naming the user, is not known to be the user's identity: a comparison with it has owner_source_untrusted not_read). owner_match is today's text match and never decides a pass. true for equality (enums.COMPARISON_OPERATORS): the row's column on one side of =, IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, or column = ANY(x) where x is one trusted session value. not_read when the row's column is related to a session identity through a construct that may or may not restrict the rows (enums.NOT_READ_RELATIONS: IN or = ANY of a subquery or a set, such as a membership lookup, IN of a list, LIKE, @>, &&, a function around the column, a cast outside enums.LOSSLESS_CASTS). false only with no such relation, or an operator that provably doesn't restrict the rows (enums.NON_RESTRICTING_OPERATORS: <>, IS DISTINCT FROM, <, >, <=, >=). Consumers use the detail fields (<x>_required, <x>_source_untrusted), never <x>_comparison alone, as isolation evidence.

tenant_comparison.description: Derived, kept for compatibility: the tri-state OR of tenant_using and tenant_with_check (true when either is true, false when both are false, not_read otherwise). The comparison is a column of the row compared with the session's tenant: a JWT claim (auth.jwt() or request.jwt.claims), a request.jwt.claim.<key> setting, a request header or cookie, or another setting, whose final key (the last JSON key, or the last dot-separated part of a setting name) is exactly one of enums.TENANT_KEYS (JSON keys compare case-sensitively; a tenant-like word anywhere else in the path does not count). true for equality (enums.COMPARISON_OPERATORS): the row's column on one side of =, IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, or column = ANY(x) where x is one trusted session value. not_read when the row's column is related to a session identity through a construct that may or may not restrict the rows (enums.NOT_READ_RELATIONS: IN or = ANY of a subquery or a set, such as a membership lookup, IN of a list, LIKE, @>, &&, a function around the column, a cast outside enums.LOSSLESS_CASTS). false only with no such relation, or an operator that provably doesn't restrict the rows (enums.NON_RESTRICTING_OPERATORS: <>, IS DISTINCT FROM, <, >, <=, >=). Consumers use the detail fields (<x>_required, <x>_source_untrusted), never <x>_comparison alone, as isolation evidence.

requires_aal2.description: The expression requires the session's authenticator assurance level to be aal2 (auth.jwt() ->> 'aal' compared with 'aal2'). Decided by the inspector, which parses the policy's expression (pg_get_expr of polqual and polwithcheck, returned by C1's query to the inspector only) as a SQL expression tree on the machine, never by a text search; the expression never leaves the machine. not_read: it couldn't be parsed, never a guess.

owner_using.description: The USING expression holds a column of the row compared with the session's user (a trusted source is one of enums.TRUSTED_OWNER_SOURCES: auth.uid(), auth.jwt() ->> 'sub', current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub'), current_setting('request.jwt.claims') ->> 'sub'; the database role name, CURRENT_USER, CURRENT_ROLE, SESSION_USER or USER (enums.UNTRUSTED_OWNER_SOURCES), or any other setting naming the user, is not known to be the user's identity: a comparison with it has owner_source_untrusted not_read). false for an insert policy (it has no USING expression). references_row.description: Every expression the policy's command is judged by (USING for a command that reads rows, the check of written rows for one that writes them) reads a column of the row (T25 B12). false: one of them reads none: a bare presence or role test (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL, auth.role() = 'authenticated', auth.jwt() IS NOT NULL), a constant comparison, true, or an absent check, which Postgres reads as true. Such a permissive policy lets every row through to the roles it names, as always_true does. not_read: an expression couldn't be parsed, or holds a subquery or a function whose body isn't read and names no column of the row (a staff lookup: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM staff WHERE user_id = auth.uid())), never a guess. Decided by the inspector from the parsed expressions, never by a text search; the expressions never leave the machine. So with false, one judged expression holds no comparison: a select, delete or insert policy has no <x>_comparison true, and an update or all policy (judged by USING and by its check) has no <x> comparison in both (T23-P1-C407: USING (user_id = auth.uid()) WITH CHECK true is owner_using true, owner_with_check false, references_row false).

owner_column.description: T29-P1-C35: the name of the row's column the policy compares with the session's user, as table_columns sends that column's name (a name the inspector hashes is hashed here too). Set only when every expression the policy's command is judged by requires one equality of that one column with a trusted user source (owner_required true, owner_source_untrusted false), and no other relation to the user appears in them; null otherwise. Schema metadata only: never a value and never the policy text. Absent from an older CLI: the evaluator then has no owner column for the table, and an open policy's fix stays guidance.

using_branches.description: T29 h4b (T29-P3-C215, P1 C155): one word per top-level OR branch of the policy's USING expression, in order (one entry with no OR; ["none"] with no USING, which Postgres reads as true). owner: the branch requires a row column to equal the session's user. member_row: an EXISTS or IN that names the session's user and ties to this row. member: one that names the session's user but not this row (a staff list). any_member: one that ties to this row but never names the session's user, so any caller meets it. signed_in: the branch reads the session but no row column (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL). row: it reads the row but not the session. none: it reads neither (true). not_read: the inspector couldn't say. An OR under an AND is one branch. null when the expression isn't parsed or has more than 8 branches. Decided from the parsed expression on the machine, never by a text search; the expression never leaves the machine. Absent from an older CLI: the evaluator judges the policy by its other fields alone.

row_rls_policies.description: One policy. The parsed comparison fields are tri-state (enums.TRI_STATE) and consistent: each <x>_comparison is the tri-state OR of <x>_using and <x>_with_check, a select or delete policy has no write check and an insert policy no USING (both false), and with no comparison <x>_required and <x>_source_untrusted are false.

query_rls_policies.description: The rls_policies query's result (up to 10000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/rls_policies.sql (C1).

public_privileges.description: Every privilege PUBLIC (every role) holds on the table or one of its live columns, from their ACLs (T21-P1-C5).

query_table_grants.description: The table_grants query's result (up to 10000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/table_grants.sql (C1).

query_table_columns.description: The table_columns query's result (up to 10000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/table_columns.sql (C1).

definer_calls.description: The functions the view runs that may read what reads leaves out (T19-P1-C131, C138, C139), reached from the view's rule, and from any view it reads in a schema that isn't a row, only through what Postgres records: BEGIN ATOMIC bodies, operators, casts, aggregates, and the CHECK functions of every domain a type holds (arrays, composite attributes, ranges). Listed: SECURITY DEFINER functions; a function whose body Postgres doesn't record (a SQL function with a string body, or any language but sql, c or internal), except Supabase's stock auth.uid, auth.role, auth.email and auth.jwt; built-ins and extension functions that run SQL text or reach another server (query_to_xml and the other *_to_xml, ts_stat, ts_rewrite with a query, dblink, crosstab, connectby); an extension's c function outside a fixed allowlist; a BEGIN ATOMIC body reading a view in such a schema or a foreign table; and a foreign table the view reads.

query_views.description: The views query's result (up to 1000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/views.sql (C1).

other_execute_roles.description: The roles other than PUBLIC that hold EXECUTE on any overload, directly or by membership in a grantee, sorted. Left out: the owner, anon, authenticated and phisc_ro, superusers, and roles that reach EXECUTE only through anon or authenticated. null past 100 names; absent or null is not read, never none (T27-P2-C59, T27-P1-C77).

query_definer_functions.description: The definer_functions query's result (up to 1000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/definer_functions.sql (C1).

auth_definers.description: Every SECURITY DEFINER function whose owner can read auth.users (a table or any column privilege, so a superuser's too), except a built-in (pg_catalog or information_schema, oid below 16384) and a trigger or event trigger function (T19-P1-C148). Postgres runs functions on a read in more places than the views' walk lists (casts, the planner, RLS policies), so any one holds auth-users-not-exposed. Up to 100, sorted.

query_exposed_schemas.description: The exposed_schemas query's result (exactly one row when ok). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/exposed_schemas.sql (C1).

query_roles.description: The roles query's result (up to 500 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/roles.sql (C1).

unconfirmed_read_policies.description: Permissive read policies on storage.objects that apply to the bucket, with no owner condition, whose reach the query can't confirm: they read another table or call a function of the app, or hold an auth wrapper the query can't read (not_read). Neither open nor limited to the owner: for a person.

file_size_limit.description: storage.buckets.file_size_limit in bytes; null when the bucket sets none.

allowed_mime_types_set.description: storage.buckets.allowed_mime_types is set and not empty (the types themselves aren't sent).

query_storage_buckets.description: The storage_buckets query's result (up to 500 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/storage_buckets.sql (C1).

query_transport.description: The transport query's result (exactly one row when ok). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/transport.sql (C1).

query_logging.description: The logging query's result (exactly one row when ok). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/logging.sql (C1).

log_parameter.description: pgaudit.log_parameter is on for this row's scope.

query_audit.description: The audit query's result (up to 500 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/audit.sql (C1).

query_self_hosted.description: The self_hosted query's result (exactly one row when ok). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/self_hosted.sql (C1).

query_advisor.description: The advisor query's result (up to 2 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/advisor.sql (C1).

row_default_acl.description: pg_default_acl, one row per (schema, object type, grantor, grantee): the privileges new objects get. schema_name null: the grantor's global default. grantee public for PUBLIC.

api_grantee.description: T19: true when the grantee is PUBLIC or an API role: anon, authenticated, or a role authenticator is a member of other than service_role (table_grants.sql's custosa_api). Absent from an older CLI: the evaluator then holds a grantee it doesn't know as a non-API role.

query_default_acl.description: The default_acl query's result (up to 2000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/default_acl.sql (C1).

row_schema_privileges.description: Every schema outside pg_catalog, information_schema and pg_toast, one row per grantee holding USAGE or CREATE on it (aclexplode of nspacl, the owner's implicit rights left out); grantee public for PUBLIC, so PUBLIC CREATE on public shows as a row.

query_schema_privileges.description: The schema_privileges query's result (up to 2000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/schema_privileges.sql (C1).

row_triggers.description: pg_trigger on tables outside the catalog, internal (constraint) triggers left out.

query_triggers.description: The triggers query's result (up to 10000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/triggers.sql (C1).

row_constraints.description: pg_constraint on tables outside the catalog, plus unique indexes that back no constraint as type unique_index (constraint_name is the index name). columns: the plain key columns in key order (for check, the columns it references). expression: some key part is an expression, so columns is not the whole key. partial: a partial index (WHERE), so it doesn't hold for every row. referenced_table: the table a foreign key references, null for every other type. NOT VALID constraints are kept (they hold for new rows); a unique index is left out only while indisready is false, and a partitioned table's ON ONLY unique index or constraint while it is invalid (relkind I).

query_constraints.description: The constraints query's result (up to 20000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/constraints.sql (C1).

row_realtime_publication.description: pg_publication_tables: every table in a logical publication (supabase_realtime is Supabase Realtime's), FOR ALL TABLES publications expanded.

query_realtime_publication.description: The realtime_publication query's result (up to 10000 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/realtime_publication.sql (C1).

row_connected_roles.description: The observed app connection role: client sessions in pg_stat_activity, other than the inspector's own, counted per (usename, application). application: application_name bucketed by the inspector's fixed table (enums.CONNECTED_APPLICATIONS); the name itself is never sent.

query_connected_roles.description: The connected_roles query's result (up to 500 rows; more is truncated with row_limit). Ships as app/knowledge/queries/connected_roles.sql (C1).

edge_function.description: One function declared in a supabase/config.toml ([functions.<name>]). entrypoint: the declared entrypoint, or the folder default <supabase dir>/functions/<name>/index.ts when none is declared, as a path relative to the root; null when the declared one resolves outside the root or can't be expressed as a path (never analysed, never read as the default). verify_jwt: the declared value; not_read when the key is absent or isn't a boolean (no default assumed).
